Multi-cause age-period-cohort model with coupled cause trends

Source: R/model-apc-causes.R
apc_causes.Rd

Forecasts the deaths of several causes together with all causes, so that the cause-specific rates add up to the all-cause rate in every draw and the trends of the causes move together as estimated. Package-specific (reference unknown): no published source of this combination is known to us.

Usage

apc_causes(
  var = "cause",
  total_level = "all",
  residual = "auto",
  age = "rw2",
  period = "rw1",
  cohort = "rw1",
  mcmc = mcmc_control(),
  resolution = c("observed", "grid"),
  shape_years = 5,
  max_refits = 1,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

var

Stratum variable with the causes.

total_level

Level of var for all causes.

residual

Add a residual cause, all deaths not covered by the listed causes: TRUE, FALSE, or "auto" (added when the listed causes leave more than 0.1% of all-cause deaths unexplained in the median cell). The residual cause is modelled but not returned.

age, period, cohort

Prior for each effect: "rw1" or "rw2". The defaults use first-order random walks for period and cohort: with second-order random walks the extrapolated trends can make forecast intervals span orders of magnitude. First-order random walks carry the last period effect forward without a trend, so forecasts are biased when mortality keeps declining. The vignette "Bayesian age-period-cohort models with bamp" compares both.

mcmc

MCMC settings from mcmc_control().

resolution

"observed" or "grid".

shape_years

Number of recent years used for the shape factors.

max_refits

Refits with longer chains if not converged.

seed

Seed of the native sampler (coherent = TRUE); NULL draws one from R's random number generator, so that set.seed() makes fits reproducible.

Value

A model specification.

Details

Model. In each group of strata that differ only in var (for example the causes of one sex), the all-cause deaths follow a binomial-logit age-period-cohort model with random-walk priors (as apc_bayes()). The cause deaths split the all-cause deaths of each cell by stick-breaking: a sequence of binomial-logit models of the share of each cause among the deaths not yet assigned, logit pi[c, i, j] = mu[c] + theta[c, i] + phi[c, j] + psi[c, k], the causes ordered by their number of deaths and the last cause taking the rest (Linderman, Johnson and Adams 2015 for the stick-breaking representation of a multinomial). The period effects of the shares have a joint random-walk prior whose precision across causes is a matrix with a Wishart prior, so that period trends of different causes can be correlated, also negatively (one cause replacing another); the cohort effects likewise. Cause rates are shares times the all-cause rate: they add up, and hazards built from them are additive. Within an age group, every cause takes the age pattern of the all-cause rate on the modelling grid.

Sources. The model is the multi-cause model of the development branch "coherent_forecasting" of bamp (bamp_multicause(), by Chris Kypridemos), rewritten here because the branch is not released; when a bamp release contains it, apc_causes() will call bamp and the native sampler will be deprecated. Changes: the exact sampler of apc_bayes(coherent = TRUE); one zero-slope constraint on the period effect of each share, only when all effects are second-order random walks (the branch also pins the cohort slope, which removes an identified trend); the all-cause model fitted with the same sampler, its period and cohort precisions with Gamma priors (Wishart priors of dimension 1); the latent-factor coupling of the branch is not taken over. Priors: Gamma(1, 0.5) for the precisions of the age effects, Wishart with C + 2 degrees of freedom and scale (1e-4 I)^-1 for the period and cohort precisions of C fields, as in the branch.

Sampler and convergence as apc_bayes() with coherent = TRUE: four chains, the Gelman-Rubin statistic of the precisions of the age effects, the diagonals of the Wishart precisions, the last period effect and the level of every field in the last year.

References

Linderman SW, Johnson MJ, Adams RP (2015). Dependent multinomial models made easy: stick-breaking with the Pólya-gamma augmentation. arXiv:1506.05843.

Schmid VJ, Held L (2007). Bayesian age-period-cohort modeling and prediction: BAMP. Journal of Statistical Software 21(8): 1-15. doi:10.18637/jss.v021.i08

See also

coda_causes() for a published model of causes of death, and reconciled() with a hierarchy of causes.

Examples

# \donttest{
x <- mt_example_causes(years = 2005:2019)
fit <- mt_fit(apc_causes(mcmc = mcmc_control("test"), seed = 1), x)
fc <- mt_forecast(fit, h = 5, n_draws = 100, seed = 1)
# }
